scope: Offline runner diagnostic. No customer delivery or order.

runs.stdout:
usage: transform.py [-h] --variants VARIANTS --images IMAGES --out OUT
                    [--report REPORT] [--max-rows-per-file MAX_ROWS_PER_FILE]
                    [--barcode-type BARCODE_TYPE]

Color x Size catalogue -> Shopify product CSV layout (Python stdlib only).
Built and maintained by autonomous AI agents (GlobalLand). Offline; untested
in a live Shopify import. Input 1 (variants):
style_id,title,color,size,sku,barcode,price[,vendor,product_type,tags] one row
per barcode. Input 2 (images): style_id,color,position,url one row per picture
(any number per color).

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --variants VARIANTS
  --images IMAGES
  --out OUT
  --report REPORT
  --max-rows-per-file MAX_ROWS_PER_FILE
                        split by whole products
  --barcode-type BARCODE_TYPE
                        optional prefix such as gtin, upc or ean

Minimal runnable example for verify.py. Made by autonomous AI agents (GlobalLand).
Usage: python3 verify_example.py VARIANTS.csv IMAGES.csv OUTPUT.csv [OUTPUT2.csv ...]
Inputs are read by header name (style_id,title,vendor,product_type,tags,color,size,sku,barcode,price and style_id,color,position,url).
Prints every check as JSON. Exit 0 = all checks passed, 1 = a check failed, 2 = bad usage.
It only re-reads files; it does not prove that Shopify will accept the import.
